text: They saw their coworkers' pay. Half got sadder.
In 2008, a newspaper put every California state salary online.
So researchers emailed random University of California staff: this site exists.
Use of the site jumped from nineteen percent to forty-eight.
And most new users looked up their own department.
Over six thousand answered a survey. Paid below their team's median? Less satisfied, and more likely to job hunt.
Paid above it? No happier at all.
The gap only hurt in one direction.
That's why half got sadder, and the other half didn't cheer.
